subject: Day 77: research solids approach
bodyText:
Today's focus
Week 12 opens the end of the first quarter, and for families on a 12-week leave, return-to-work week. Solids are still 1 to 3 months out, but deciding the approach now, while you have bandwidth, beats deciding in the high chair.

Action items
- Start researching baby-led weaning versus purees for the 4-to-6-month start and decide as a couple before the window opens; the evidence shows no difference in choking risk between the two methods, so this is about logistics and preference, not safety. AAP HealthyChildren, starting solid foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Note the three readiness signals you will look for around 6 months: sitting with minimal support, loss of the tongue-thrust reflex, and active interest in food. AAP HealthyChildren, starting solid foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Get the pumping schedule operational if Anoushka is back at work: about three sessions per 8-hour day, 15 to 20 minutes each, refrigerated immediately and frozen the same day if not used within four days.
- Pack the daycare or nanny bag the night before with labeled bottles, extra outfits, diapers, and a sleep sack, and confirm the communication channel the provider uses.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Daycare or nanny adjustment fussiness for one to two weeks at the start; frequent minor illness in the first two months of group care is expected.
- [monitor] Sleep starting to fragment with more frequent night wakings; note the date it begins, as it may mark the early 4-month regression.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting beyond 24 hours, or crying clearly disproportionate to the handoff that does not settle.
- [call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher under 90 days, apnea, or a color change during sleep is a same-day call, and 911 for blue lips or labored breathing!

Enrichment opportunities
- Place toys at varying distances during tummy time toward 75 to 90 minutes cumulative, staggered into short bouts, to motivate scooting and pivoting. AAP HealthyChildren, tummy to play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Live-sing across varied tempos during play, moving slow to fast to slow, since participatory singing, not recordings, is the active ingredient for perceptual and communicative gains. Gerry et al. 2012, active music in infancy: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Spend a few minutes hiding a toy partly under a blanket and watch whether he reaches for the visible part; this is an early object-permanence precursor that consolidates around 8 to 10 months.

Upcoming
- Day 84-91: sleep consolidation window opens (~3 months); set the consistent sleep-wake routine
- Months 4-6: target window for starting solids; allergen introduction window opens around month 4
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit; vaccines RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
